title: Locals protest outside Manipur Chief Minister's residence in Imphal over killings

tea.why: Locals protested the killing of two men by suspected militants while they were collecting firewood near the Imphal East and Kangpokpi border.
tea.want: The protesters sought to highlight the ongoing violence in the state by placing the bodies of the deceased outside the Chief Minister's residence.
tea.changed: Oct 19: Police used tear gas to disperse protesters who had placed bodies outside the Chief Minister's bungalow in Imphal.

summary: On October 19, 2026, a group of locals gathered outside the residence of Manipur Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh in Imphal to protest the deaths of two men. The deceased, identified as Arubam Ronil and Lairenlakpam Inaobi, were allegedly killed by suspected militants while collecting firewood near the border of Imphal East and Kangpokpi districts. Protesters placed the bodies of the victims at the gate of the Chief Minister's bungalow to express their anger regarding the ongoing violence in the region. In response, security personnel stationed at the residence deployed tear gas to disperse the crowd. Following the intervention, the bodies were transported to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences. Officials reported that four other individuals were injured and three remain missing following the initial ambush.
demands: Accountability for the killing of firewood collectors
response: Security personnel stationed at the Chief Minister's residence fired several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the protesters, according to police officials.
